arStrings.szText: Tragic as the slaughter of his family was, it was another step on Deckard’s path to becoming Horadrim. For what are we without the common folk we strive to protect?
At last, Cain set down his research and took up his staff. He forged friendships with Tristram’s townfolk.
He writes of Pepin the healer, who was “kinder to all than many deserved,” and of Griswold the smith, “loud as an ox but gentle as a bird.”
This staff—one of a chosen time-tested few—is a relic from those relatively happy days before Tristram’s darkening.
